notes: The RULE-OVER-CONSTANT upgrade: the ceiling is DERIVED from the BOM, never a free constant -- adopt a high-Tg laminate or 125C-rated capacitors and the ceiling re-derives for free (re-run min-of-BOM; the research doc's stated threshold). The instantiated value for the CURRENT BOM is thermal.gates.t_max_ceiling, citing the bom.rating.* sub-facts. Steady-state target <= ceiling - transient allowance keeps the +20C transient from ever exceeding the ceiling (105-20=85C target).

source.ref: docs/research/thermal-gates-derivation-2026-06-10.md #constant-2: min-of-BOM instantiation; floor part = the 105C aluminum electrolytic capacitor (bom.rating.cap_electrolytic_105c), matched by the connector housing rating (bom.rating.connector_minifit_105c); FR-4 ~110C continuous and Schottky TJ 125C sit above

notes: The CURRENT-BOM instantiation of thermal.gates.t_max_rule -- a derived param citing the Class A sub-facts bom.rating.cap_electrolytic_105c / bom.rating.schottky_tj_125c / bom.rating.fr4_continuous_110c / bom.rating.connector_minifit_105c (min = 105). Effectively ZERO explicit margin against the cap, ~5C against FR-4 continuous -- which is why the steady-state TARGET is 85C (ceiling - 20C transient) and the operating point 80C keeps cap life in the multi-thousand-hour range (Arrhenius: ~11,300 h at 80C vs 2,000 h at 105C). Changes ONLY by re-running min-of-BOM (the rule entry), never by edit. Hand default today: cec_synth_pipeline physics_gates T_max_C=105.

source.ref: docs/research/thermal-gates-derivation-2026-06-10.md #constant-3: +20C has no meaning without a time constant; trace tau ~1-10 s (fine traces) to ~100 s (board mass, IEEE SEMI-THERM); first-order model dT(t)=dT_final*(1-e^(-t/tau)); a 0.5 s event at tau 2-5 s reaches only ~9-22% of dT_final (recomputed 2026-06-10 panel: 1-e^(-0.5/5)=9.5%, 1-e^(-0.5/2)=22%; the doc's ~10-25% rounds)

notes: The (dT, tau) PAIRS replacing the bare +20C allowance. Fault-DURATION facts are datasheet/standard-pinned Class A sub-facts (fault.duration.*); the TAU VALUES are derivation-class pending bench -- OQ (cluster-2 metrology): measure trace thermal tau with a current step on a populated lane -> CL-13 label upgrades tau to Class C. The slowest mandatory protection (PSU OCP <=500 ms) sits well inside trace tau, so copper never reaches steady state during a cleared fault -- the +20C budget covers exactly the near-threshold ~500 ms case. Hand default today: cec_synth_pipeline physics_gates T_max_transient_C = T_max+20.

Conservative direction (the 30C-rise allowable would be HIGHER), so 75 is safe as the 30C gate -- but it must never be read as a 30C-validated figure; re-derive from the IPC-2152 via appendix at 30C rise when acquired. Vias run 20-30% hotter than an equal-area surface trace (embedded in FR-4). Part of retiring the flat J_max=100: at promotion the three thermal.jmax.* entries supersede the flat hand gate (physics_gates J_max_A_mm2=100 tombstones in that PR).

source.ref: docs/research/thermal-gates-derivation-2026-06-10.md #constant-4: from I = k*dT^0.44*A^0.725 (IPC-2221, k=0.048 external -- the corpus thermal.k_ipc.external param) density falls as area grows; worked public point (smps.us, 2152-CHART-derived): 10 A at 20C rise -> ~0.32 mm2 -> ~31 A/mm2; allowable density at the 30C operating rise is order 35-60 A/mm2 for the boards' 1-10 A conductors

notes: Density-split member, ceiling for EXTERNAL traces at the 30C rise -- SCALE-DEPENDENT (the 0.725 exponent: smaller, higher-rise traces legitimately run higher; this is the 1-10 A conductor class the boards carry). CHART-FAMILY DISAMBIGUATION (2026-06-10 panel, coherence seat; re-verified): the smps.us 31 A/mm2 point and the k=0.048 formula are DIFFERENT chart families that BRACKET the answer -- the IPC-2221 closed form at the same 10 A/20C condition gives ~0.165 mm2 -> ~60 A/mm2, and at the 30C operating rise ~77 A/mm2; the chosen 60 is the conservative end of the doc's 35-60 bracket and sits ~22% under the 2221 closed form at 30C. Flat 100 A/mm2 is NON-CONSERVATIVE here and is retired by this split at promotion. Derivation-class: VERIFY against IPC-2152 Figure 5-2 at 30C rise when acquired (upgrade trigger H->A). Formula params already Class A: thermal.k_ipc.external.

notes: Density-split member, ceiling for INTERNAL traces at the 30C rise. Deliberately keeps the conservative side of the documented 2221-vs-2152 internal-conductor disagreement (the halving rule had no empirical backing; 2152 measured internal traces nearer free-air -- the conservative LOWER density is kept until the standard is acquired). value.validity: adiabatic: valid for pulses < 1 s, conservative to 10 s -- NOTE cooling effects can erode the adiabatic assumption from as little as 1-2 s (Adam), so the 1-10 s span is a narrowing conservative bound, not a validated window; beyond 10 s revert to steady-state ampacity

source.ref: Onderdonk adiabatic fusing relation, t = 0.0346*(A/I)^2 (A in mil2; I2t form), via Brooks/Adam UltraCAD papers and Babrauskas (earliest published: Stauffacher 1928); Preece steady-fusing cross-check I = a*d^1.5; derivation and J-t table: docs/research/thermal-gates-derivation-2026-06-10.md #constant-5. Fully public -- NO IPC verify-note needed (only the underlying test method TM-650 2.5.4.1A is IPC)

notes: The flat 400 A/mm2 hand gate CONVERTED to the (J, t) curve it silently was: 400 A/mm2 IS the Onderdonk melting density for a ~0.5 s adiabatic pulse from a 20C start (~381 from 80C; elevated start costs ~7%, factor 0.93). RESEARCH-DOC ERRATUM (2026-06-10 panel, coherence seat; independently re-verified): the doc's ~0.94 factor matches the 70C end of its own '70-80C' bracket -- at exactly 80C the Onderdonk log term gives sqrt(0.6226/0.7148)=0.933, so 0.93 is recorded (the conservative AND correct value; the doc's table row '~385' correspondingly reads ~381). CLAUSES (owner-enumerated): (1) BACKSTOP ONLY -- Brooks/Adam simulation shows real traces fuse 1.5-6x SLOWER than Onderdonk predicts, so the curve is conservative; it is a do-not-exceed forensic backstop and NEVER justifies smaller copper; (2) operating density is ~5-12x below the fusing density even at the slowest 500 ms protection window, so platform protection (TPS2121 us-ms, PSU OCP <=500 ms) clears faults long before copper melts -- if protection is ever slower than ~1 s (PPTC near I_trip), the curve becomes design-relevant: size copper so operating density >= 3x below fusing at the actual clearing time. CLASS TYPING (panel-adjudicated): Class A KEPT against a refuter downgrade-to-H -- the doc's Caveats explicitly rule Onderdonk/Preece 'fully public and NOT derivation-class'; the authority is PUBLISHED ENGINEERING LITERATURE (Onderdonk via Brooks/Adam, Babrauskas, Stauffacher 1928), not a standards-body document -- source.type 'standard' is the closest vocabulary fit, recorded as such. The fused-board service rule stands separately as service.fused_board_retirement. Hand default today: cec_synth_pipeline physics_gates J_fuse_A_mm2=400 (tombstones at promotion in favor of the curve). Status proposed: judge-visible only; per lint the physics consumer skips it until *_validated/human_approved -- the binding act is the status move + promotion, never this draft.

notes: Operational rule, its own one-line H (owner option taken): a board that has experienced a copper fusing event NEVER returns to service -- fusing is destructive and one-time; adjacent copper, laminate, and joints are suspect even where visually intact.
